page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor utilizing x86_64 architecture. The server delivers 32 virtual CPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside instruction support for AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX-512 VNNI), and AES-NI.

The server does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage for disk persistence. Network performance features a baseline throughput of 10 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

In benchmark testing, the ecs.g6.8xlarge shows solid mid-tier multi-threaded compute and memory capabilities, offset by lower single-core throughput. Single-threaded performance falls into the lower quartile, observed in stress-ng single-core tests (1311.98) and gzip compression (22.62 GB/sec). Conversely, parallel workloads scale predictably into middle-tier performance profiles, supported by PassMark CPU results (27100.23), Geekbench multi-core scores (10179.0), and stress-ng multi-core metrics (28006.29). Memory throughput demonstrates 108.04 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 47.67 GB/sec for writes.

This hardware balance makes the ecs.g6.8xlarge well configured for horizontally scaled enterprise applications, relational and in-memory databases, continuous integration tasks, and high-concurrency static web serving. Workloads heavily constrained by single-thread latency or demanding raw local disk I/O may require different instance architectures.
